requirements.text: She is currently working from the Bengaluru office in Karnataka, and the asset should be recorded under TechCorp India operations
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 'LOC_004' AND city = 'Bengaluru' AND state = 'Karnataka' AND country IN ('India', 'IN') AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: the seed has no Bengaluru location (LOC_001 New York, LOC_002 London, LOC_003 San Francisco), so the office must be added with add_location before the asset can be recorded there; id assumed next in sequence (LOC_004 after LOC_003), as the original CMDB check's location_id = LOC_004 also implies
country is not named; Bengaluru, Karnataka and 'TechCorp India' fix it as India, and the column is NOT NULL
'TechCorp India operations' is not a separate organisation in the seed; TechCorp is ORG_001, Aisha's own org, and no tool creates an organisation
name is free text and untested; no original check tests the location row

disagreement: country: A IN ('India', 'IN'), B 'India'; chose A's because the request never names the country and the seed's style ('USA', 'UK') fixes neither the full name nor a code, so either spelling is a correct answer

requirements.text: Please add this device to the item records
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_005' AND serial_number = 'DESKTOP-IN-781' AND owner_id = 'USER_004' AND location_id = 'LOC_004' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND status = 'in_use' AND cost = 78000
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (CI_005 after CI_004)
owner is Aisha = USER_004 (Aisha Williams, the only Aisha in the seed); policy 5.1 requires a recorded owner_id
'approximately 78 grand' in rupees is cost 78000; the request gives no exact figure and the cost column has no currency
org_id ORG_001 added to the original check's cells because the request asks for the record 'under TechCorp India operations'
the processor, RAM, SSD and graphics details have no column in configuration_item and are untested; the name is free text

requirements.text: she would like to raise an incident for a required software installation, with the impact set to medium, but it is not business critical
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_004' AND configuration_item = 'CI_005' AND status = 'new' AND category = 'software' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'low' AND priority = 'low'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023)
'not business critical' read as urgency low, as the original check has it
priority low from policy 3.1's matrix (impact medium, urgency low), added to the original check's cells
category software from 'software installation' (category is NOT NULL and software is a seed value), added to the original check's cells
the incident is linked to the new desktop CI_005 as the original check has it; the request raises it in the same breath as the device
this policy version sets no channel default, so channel is untested; status new from policy 3.1's default

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the three create requirements (same tables, anchors and cells apart from the country predicate) and on both dispositions. disagreement: stay on CI_002 'Aisha Desktop' (B only, as the boundary of 'Aisha's desktop'); dropped because no tool in the task updates a CI (register_configuration_item only creates), the mistaken reading, linking the incident to CI_002 instead of the new device, is already caught by the incident requirement's configuration_item = CI_005, and the serial DESKTOP-NYC-145 does not nearly match DESKTOP-IN-781. disagreement: location country predicate (logged in the requirement). disagreement: location text: A quotes both the office clause and 'recorded under TechCorp India operations', B only the office; kept A's because the org_id cell comes from the second clause. Both original checks are kept with extra cells: org_id on the CI (asked by 'recorded under TechCorp India operations') and category plus priority on the incident (from the request's wording and the policy matrix). The Bengaluru location is a new requirement because the original check's location_id = LOC_004 presupposes it and the tools include add_location. Aisha's users.location_id (LOC_001) is not asked to change and no tool writes users. This policy version names opened_by as a mandatory incident input, but the request does not say whether Aisha or the acting user opens it, so it is not tested. Policy 7's knowledge search has no tool here and no matching article (KB_003 is desktop boot failure); left out.
